issues.legal_issue: A pending exemption does not suspend an express tender deadline for furnishing a bank guarantee when the tender makes the deadline independent of the exemption.
material_facts: The successful bidder received confirmation of its tender, which required bank guarantees within ten days.
The tender did not make the guarantee deadline conditional on obtaining an exemption notification.
The bidder did not furnish the guarantees, and sought to rely on the absence of the notification.
The tender covered individual plots below the statutory ceiling, and the bidder had earlier sought registration of the sale deeds without treating the notification as a prerequisite.
issues.conclusion: The exemption notification was not a condition precedent to furnishing the bank guarantees, and its absence did not entitle the bidder to further time.
issues.legal_principle: Section 81(3)(b) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 empowers the Government to exempt land by Gazette notification, subject to conditions; it does not itself alter a separate contractual deadline. The express tender terms governed. The Court relied on the principles in Har Shankar v. Deputy Excise and Taxation Commissioner and New Bihar Biri Leaves Co. v. State of Bihar that parties who accept contractual terms must accept their burdens as well as their benefits, and on Assistant Excise Commissioner v. Isaac Peter that administrative fairness cannot be used to alter express contractual terms.

rule.if: public_tender_contract_dispute and bidder_received_confirmation and tender_sets_guarantee_deadline and not tender_makes_deadline_conditional_on_exemption

predicates.public_tender_contract_dispute: The dispute arises from a public tender contract and its enforcement.
predicates.bidder_received_confirmation: The successful bidder received confirmation of its tender.
predicates.tender_sets_guarantee_deadline: The tender specified a deadline for the successful bidder to furnish a bank guarantee.
predicates.tender_makes_deadline_conditional_on_exe: The tender expressly made the guarantee deadline conditional on an exemption being granted.

issues.definition: When a public tender sets a guarantee deadline after confirmation without making that deadline conditional on an exemption, the exemption does not postpone the guarantee obligation.

issues.legal_issue: A tender contract is not unenforceable merely because an exemption notification has not been issued before the tender, where the contract has not yet transferred an interest in the land.
material_facts: The Government had permitted the development authority to sell the land, and the tender was issued before the exemption notification was published.
The notification was published after the tender confirmations but before any sale deed or transfer of title to the successful bidder.
The agreement contemplated registration of the sale deed and delivery of possession only after payment of the full land value.
The bidder relied on Sections 87 and 23 to contend that the contract was unenforceable or unlawful.
issues.conclusion: Section 87 did not make the contract unenforceable, and the absence of the exemption notification before the tender did not make the contract void under Section 23 of the Contract Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 87 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 concerns land acquired after the notified date and the consequences when a person thereby holds land exceeding the ceiling; an agreement for sale does not itself transfer title or create an interest in the property. Section 81(3)(b) provides for exemption by Gazette notification. Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 did not apply to invalidate this contract in the circumstances. The Court distinguished contractual obligations from the later statutory consequences attached to acquiring and continuing to hold land.

predicates.public_tender_contract_dispute: The dispute concerns the enforceability of a contract formed through a public tender.
predicates.agreement_for_sale_only: The parties had an agreement for sale, with transfer of the land to occur later.
predicates.no_title_or_interest_transferred_before_: No title or interest in the land had passed to the bidder before the exemption was granted.

issues.definition: Where a public tender results only in an agreement for a later sale and no land interest has yet passed, a pending exemption does not by itself invalidate the contract.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not imply a contractual term that conflicts with an express tender condition or use administrative fairness to rewrite that condition.
material_facts: The written tender specified when the successful bidder had to furnish bank guarantees and the consequences of non-compliance.
The High Court treated the exemption notification as an implied term that postponed the guarantee deadline.
The parties had not agreed that performance of the guarantee obligation would await the exemption notification.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not imply a term postponing the deadline because that would modify a vital express term of the tender.
issues.legal_principle: An implied term must be necessary, consistent with the express contract, and not merely reasonable or convenient. The Court relied on Assistant Excise Commissioner v. Isaac Peter for the rule that administrative-law fairness cannot vary express contractual terms; on W.B. State Electricity Board v. Patel Engineering Co. for strict adherence to tender conditions; and on the tender-review principles in Tata Cellular, Directorate of Education v. Educomp Datamatics, Air India v. Cochin International Airport and Monarch Infrastructure v. Commissioner, Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation.

predicates.public_tender_contract_dispute: The dispute concerns the terms or enforcement of a public tender contract.
predicates.written_tender_has_express_deadline: The written tender expressly set a deadline for a required act by the successful bidder.
predicates.proposed_implied_term_conflicts_with_exp: A party asks the court to imply a term that would postpone or otherwise contradict the express deadline.

issues.definition: When a written public tender sets an express deadline, a conflicting implied term cannot be used to extend it.

issues.legal_issue: A tender may be cancelled when the successful bidder fails to meet an express bank-guarantee requirement within the specified time.
material_facts: The tender required the successful bidder to provide bank guarantees within ten days of receiving the confirmation letter.
The tender stated that failure to comply would result in cancellation and forfeiture of the earnest money deposit.
The bidder did not furnish the guarantees, and the development authority cancelled the confirmation and later ratified that cancellation.
The High Court held the cancellation illegal, but the Supreme Court rejected the basis for that decision.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation for failure to furnish the required bank guarantees was not invalid merely because the exemption notification had not been issued, and the High Court's contrary judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The express tender terms govern the bidder's obligation and the consequence of non-compliance; a court cannot substitute a different deadline by implying a term. The Court applied the tender-adherence principles in W.B. State Electricity Board v. Patel Engineering Co. and the contractual principles in Har Shankar v. Deputy Excise and Taxation Commissioner and Assistant Excise Commissioner v. Isaac Peter.

predicates.public_tender_contract_dispute: The dispute concerns cancellation of a successful bid in a public tender.
predicates.tender_requires_guarantee_after_confirma: The tender required the successful bidder to provide a bank guarantee after receiving confirmation.
predicates.bidder_fails_to_furnish_guarantee_by_dea: The successful bidder did not provide the required guarantee by the tender deadline.
predicates.tender_provides_cancellation_for_failure: The tender specified cancellation as a consequence of failing to provide the required guarantee.

issues.definition: When a successful bidder misses an express guarantee deadline and the tender provides for cancellation on that failure, the cancellation is upheld.
